Starlight Park: the stars at one light-year to the metre

A theme park at night where every star is a light bulb at its real place. The Sun is a glint on a desk. Around it, every star you can see with the naked eye, and every star within 81 light-years, stands in its real direction at its real distance: Proxima Centauri 4.2 m away, Sirius 8.6 m, Vega 25 m, Polaris 433 m, Betelgeuse 500 m, the centre of the Milky Way 26.7 km straight ahead. Each shines as bright as it would from where you stand: at the desk the sky is our night sky; walk away and the constellations come apart. The ground is the plane of the Milky Way; the Oort cloud is a haze 1.6 m round the desk.

There is no ground: platforms float by the stars. Walkways join the nearest stars; a bike on the hub takes trails to stars up to a kilometre away (Betelgeuse is a 500 m ride); a car in the car park takes roads to places kilometres off, as far as the Large Magellanic Cloud, 163 km, on autopilot: choose where when you get on. Every named star has a platform the car can reach; a helicopter on the helipad flies to stars 30 m to 1.5 km away; a jet at the airport flies to runways at the galactic centre, by the black hole, and the Large Magellanic Cloud. Every constellation has an attraction sized to it, running through its brightest stars: model railways (the Big Dipper's), roller coasters, sky rides, monorails, maglev trains. Each ends beside a familiar object at real size, so you can judge the distance: a lamppost, a school bus, the Betelgeuse house, a lighthouse, a skyscraper, a mountain.

The stars themselves are far too small to see at this scale: the Sun is 147 nm across, the size of a flu virus. So each platform has the instrument it would take: an electron microscope at the desk, light microscopes for the big stars (Betelgeuse is the width of a hair). E beside one to look; in VR, lean into a light microscope's eyepiece. Sitting or standing: the button at the bottom right, or click the left stick in VR.

WASD walk  ·  drag to look  ·  shift faster  ·  E beside the bike or car to get on and choose where (WS and E in the list; E again on the way for stop or get off), or info on what you look at  ·  F fly (space / C up and down, =− speed)  ·  T teleport  ·  C constellation lines  ·  P hide / show paths  ·  O hide / show attractions  ·  L labels  ·  H readout  ·  R back to the desk
In VR: left stick walk (left trigger faster; up/down in the bike or car list), right stick turn, A or right trigger: get on and choose / info, B closes a list, B fly (right stick up/down to climb), X labels, Y constellation lines, click the right stick: hide / show paths, click the left stick: seated; teleport from the panel on your left wrist (point and pull the right trigger)
